summary.text: Translation is how cells build proteins, using RNA molecules as templates.
Ribosomes read messenger RNA three nucleotides at a time, and each triple adds one specific amino acid to the chain.
Transfer RNAs carry the amino acids to the ribosome, pairing their anticodon with the matching codon on the mRNA.

facts.label: Genetic code
facts.value: The matching from nucleotide triple to amino acid

facts.label: Ribosome parts
facts.value: Eukaryote ribosomes have a small 40S and large 60S subunit

facts.label: tRNA size
facts.value: Small non-coding RNAs, 74 to 93 nucleotides long

facts.label: Location
facts.value: mRNA is decoded in a ribosome, outside the nucleus

items.prompt: An mRNA has 12 nucleotides in a row. Read in triples, how many amino acids are added?
items.explain: Nucleotides are read three at a time and each triple adds one amino acid, so 12 nucleotides give 4.

items.prompt: A transfer RNA with an amino acid attached arrives at the ribosome. What is its role there?

options.label: It carries the gene's instructions from the chromosome
It forms the ribosome's two subunits
It links amino acids into a protein on its own
It delivers its amino acid, pairing its anticodon with a matching codon

items.explain: tRNAs carry specific amino acids and bind mRNA codons through their anticodons, while mRNA carries the instructions from the chromosomes.

items.prompt: An enzyme attaches the wrong amino acid to a tRNA. What can result?

options.label: An inappropriate amino acid at that position in the protein
The mRNA codon changes to fit the new amino acid
The ribosome refuses to start translation
The tRNA's anticodon changes to fit

items.explain: Mispairing tRNAs with the wrong amino acids can put inappropriate amino acids into the protein.

items.prompt: Two mRNA molecules differ in the order of their nucleotide triplets. What changes in the protein?

options.label: The number of subunits in the ribosome
Which cell the finished protein is sent to
The order of the amino acids in the chain
The attachment site on the tRNA

items.explain: The sequence of nucleotides in the mRNA determines the sequence of amino acids.

items.prompt: A polypeptide is still being made. Can it already begin folding?

options.label: No, folding starts only once the ribosome finishes
No, folding happens only outside the cell
Yes, but only after the mRNA is destroyed
Yes, it can start folding during synthesis

items.explain: The polypeptide later folds into an active protein, and it can also start folding during protein synthesis.

items.prompt: Why do the two ribosome subunits join before translation?

options.label: To cut the mRNA into triplets
To make a place where the polypeptide can be produced
To attach amino acids to the tRNAs
To carry the mRNA out of the nucleus

items.explain: The subunits come together to provide a location for translation and a polypeptide to be produced.

paragraphs.heading: What it is
paragraphs.text: Translation is how cells make proteins, using RNA molecules as templates. The protein is a chain of amino acids, and their order is set by the order of nucleotides in the RNA. The work is done by ribosomes, large complexes of RNA and proteins. The finished chain, called a polypeptide, folds into a working protein, and it can even begin folding while it is still being made.

paragraphs.heading: Reading in threes
paragraphs.text: The RNA is read three nucleotides at a time. Each group of three, called a codon, adds one particular amino acid to the growing chain. The matching of codons to amino acids is the genetic code. Because each new amino acid matches the next codon along the messenger RNA (mRNA), the order of the codons decides the order of the amino acids.

paragraphs.heading: The protein factory
paragraphs.text: Messenger RNA carries genetic information from the chromosomes to the ribosomes, which work outside the nucleus. A ribosome is the cell's factory for assembling amino acids into proteins. In eukaryotes it has two parts, a small 40S subunit and a large 60S subunit. These come together before translation begins, giving the work a place to happen.

paragraphs.heading: Transfer RNA, the carrier
paragraphs.text: Amino acids are brought to the ribosome by transfer RNA (tRNA), small RNA chains of 74 to 93 nucleotides. Each tRNA has a spot to hold an amino acid and an anticodon, a three-nucleotide sequence that pairs with the matching codon on the mRNA. Enzymes called aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases attach the right amino acid to each tRNA, which is then said to be charged. If they attach the wrong one, the protein can end up with an incorrect amino acid. This mistranslation happens at low levels in most organisms.

paragraphs.heading: Inside the ribosome
paragraphs.text: Translation has three stages: initiation, elongation and termination. The ribosome has two binding sites for tRNA. The A site takes in an incoming tRNA whose anticodon matches the codon, and the P/E site holds the tRNA attached to the growing chain. The ribosome moves along the mRNA toward its 3' end. Each new amino acid joins at the end of the chain called the C-terminus, which is why translation is described as running from amine to carboxyl.
